children: reported mixed results for the second quarter, beating on the bottom-line but missing on the top-line and setting downbeat guidance for the current quarter and full year, all of which resulted in a double-digit decline in the share price into Thursday’s open.

“While the environment remains dynamic, we are appropriately measured in our outlook for the balance of the year,” said Lovesac CEO Shawn David Nelson. “We are underway with our most prolific year of new product introductions—a roadmap we believe will build through the second half and meaningfully strengthen our position entering fiscal 2028.”

Until then, Lovesac expects to slip back into the red in the third quarter with a loss of $0.62 to $0.83 per share compared to estimates for a loss of $0.54 despite earning a profit of $0.51 per share in Q2. However, this was largely achieved from $21M in IEEPA tariff refunds and interest.
Excluding this benefit, adjusted EBITDA reversed the $800M gain in the same quarter last year to a loss of $1.3M in the current second quarter.
Shares are also weighed down by negative comparable sales, a less than expected increase in total sales, and margin compression excluding the 1,240 basis points impact from refunded tariffs.

sees net sales within a range of $140M to $150M versus $156.87M estimates. Additionally, the company expects a net loss of $9M to $10M and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $7M to $10M versus expectations for an adjusted EBITDA loss of $5.26M.

For the full year, net sales are seen to be between $690M and $710M versus $717.3M estimates. Net income is expected to be between $14.5M and $18.5M, or $0.98 to $1.26 per share versus $0.56 per share estimates. Again, the profit outlook is distorted by the $21M of tariff refunds collected this year.

title: Lovesac tumbles as tariff refund masks underlying Q2 weakness
